scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being a "nass" (which I think is slang for "n**a" but I'm not entirely sure) in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, my wife and I didn't do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she really wanted was for me not to see her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed to that. She kept telling me she knew I'd love it, and she loved it too. She and her best friend, who was the maid of honor, kept sharing these reaction posts of grooms crying when they first see their bride, tagging me in them and saying, "This will be you!" So, I guess she expected me to have a strong emotional reaction when she walked down. On the day of the wedding, she looked beautiful, as always. But honestly, I didn't think the dress was flattering on her. I didn't focus on that though; I focused on her. I smiled, but I didn't break down into tears like some of those reaction pictures and videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me, trying to get me to look at her and mouthed "stop." We got married, kissed, and everything was fine at the reception. After our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend, and apparently, there were pictures where I didn't look how she pictured. She asked if I wanted me to cry, and I said no, but she was disappointed because it was such a big day, and she thought I would have a stronger reaction. I told her I was ecstatic to marry her, and that showed without being overly dramatic. I also mentioned that her friend was nudging me the whole time, which I felt was unfair. Then I asked if we had a wedding or a play because I never got any lines. Now she's mad at me. I do feel bad that she's disappointed, but I couldn't force myself to have that reaction. So, am I being a nass here? I don't think so. I was honest about my feelings, and I focused on her instead of the dress. I didn't understand why she expected me to cry, especially since I didn't think the dress was that great. Plus, her friend was pushing me to react, which made it harder for me to just enjoy the moment. I think I handled it as best as I could, but maybe I should have been more understanding of her expectations. Wait, maybe I should have tried to be more emotional for her sake. Even if I didn't feel like crying, maybe I should have put on a show because it was her big day. But then again, I don't want to fake emotions. That seems insincere. I guess the line is tricky. I want to support her, but I also don't want to pretend to feel something I don't. I also wonder if cultural or traditional expectations played a role here. In some cultures, the groom's emotional reaction is a big part of the wedding, and maybe she felt let down because of that. I should consider that perspective too. Maybe I could have communicated better beforehand about my feelings regarding the dress and the emotional aspect. In the end, I think I did what I thought was right, but perhaps I could have been more considerate of her expectations. It's a tough spot because I don't want to compromise my authenticity, but I also want to make her happy on her wedding day. Maybe we can talk about it and find a middle ground where both of our feelings are respected.
